test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Out of the blue
solution:
The correct answer is **'completely unexpectedly'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Out of the blue'** means without warning or unexpectedly.
 
• Example- She called me **out of the blue.**
 
• It is clear that **'completely unexpected'** is the most appropriate meaning among the options for the given idiom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drop a bombshell**- To make an unexpected announcement that will change the situation.
 
• Example- The chairman **dropped a bombshell** when he announced a merger with the company's biggest rival.
 
• **Jaw drop**- Showing total amazement.
 
• Example- When the prize was announced, the winner's **jaw dropped**.
